author: fitzgerald
imp: Build long sentences as accumulating clauses joined by dashes and semicolons, letting each addition heighten the one before until the line resolves on a single cadenced beat ('a promise that she had done gay, exciting things just a while since').
Anchor every abstraction in a concrete, slightly extravagant image: render hope as 'an extraordinary gift,' a green light, 'the silver pepper of the stars,' never as bare statement.
Pair romantic beauty with quiet irony in the same breath, so admiration and disenchantment coexist ('his count of enchanted objects had diminished by one').
Observe wealth and class with a precise, faintly appalled exactness: name the polo ponies, the forty acres of lawn, the eighty dollars a month, the rented mansions.
Treat voices, gestures, and light as carriers of meaning; let a tone of voice ('a deathless song') reveal character more than any explicit claim.
Keep the narrator reserved and self-aware, withholding judgement while letting his refusals to judge become their own commentary.
Reach for the elegiac whenever the scene touches time, loss, or the past, ending such passages on a falling, valedictory rhythm.
Use color and weather as emotional weather: rain for dread, sudden sunshine for joy, gold and white for desire and money commingled.
Let dialogue stay clipped, mannered, and evasive while the narration around it does the lyrical and moral work.
Deploy precise, unexpected adjectives in unusual pairings ('riotous excursions,' 'turbulent emotions,' 'unaffected scorn'), avoiding the obvious modifier.
Render the very rich as enchanting and faintly sinister at once, careless people moving behind glass and money.
Introduce flashes of irony or comedy through small grotesque details (the butler's nose, the spitting maid) to puncture the glamour you have just raised.
Build paragraphs toward a final clause that turns observation into aphorism or quiet wisdom ('Reserving judgements is a matter of infinite hope').
Prefer the cadence of yearning to resolution: leave desire unconsummated, the light still burning, the boat beating on against the current.
